text:
Maya Chen: Hey team — heads up from Atlas: they can only ship 8 of 12 H100s this week due to allocation. They propose a split: 8 by air (expedite), 4 by sea next month. Need quick decision on earmarking and the return-label flow for any DOA units. ETA options?

Chris Patel: Can we push for 10 air? What's the cost delta vs 8 air?

Lia (AtlasVendor): Sorry for the squeeze — confirmed 8 air available with AWBs today, remaining 4 would go ocean. Air surcharge +$7,000/unit. If you accept the 4-unit sea delay we can offer a $4,000/unit credit on those 4.

Nate O'Connor: We need at least 10 in EU for Monday deployments. Any customs/EORI blockers if we split shipments?

Lia (AtlasVendor): EU warehouse has 5 intake slots this week. Air into FRA can clear in 24–48h. Sea ETA earliest May 22. For split shipments, we can consolidate the 4 into an existing container to reduce cost but that'll be the delay. No EORI mismatch on our side but need your importer EORI on the AWB.

Sana Ruiz: Ops Q — for DOA RMA, what's the return-label flow? Logistics needs prepaid returns to avoid staging delays at the depot.

FreightCo-Rep: We can provide prepaid return labels for the air shipments (prepaid AWB return). Sea returns require depot RMA, pallet rework, and additional dock fees — billable if not covered by Atlas.

ops-bot: Auto-check — current reserved EU capacity next week: 12 GPUs free. If 10 arrive by Friday 18:00 UTC we can schedule deployment.

Zoe Park: If we accept 8 air + 4 sea, can 2 of the sea units be rerouted to NL dedicated DC on arrival? We need serial tracking & manifest adjustments.

Maya Chen: Lia — can you provide serial ranges and provisional AWB numbers for the 8 air units? Also request confirmation of prepaid RMA labels for DOA and a formal credit proposal for the sea delay.

Lia (AtlasVendor): Manifest snippet below (partial):
```
AWB: 125-ACX-9987, 125-ACX-9988, ...
Air SNs: H100-02A-1001 -> H100-02A-1008
Sea SNs: H100-02A-1009 -> H100-02A-1012
Container (sea): CNL-3957
```
We will issue provisional credit of $4,000/unit on the 4 sea units if you accept mixed shipping. Prepaid RMA labels for the air shipments: yes. Sea RMAs require depot processing.

Chris Patel: Quick finance calc pls: air surcharge vs credit nets to what? Also add potential depot/pallet costs for the sea units.

Maya Chen: Quick numbers: air surcharge = +$56k (8 * $7k). Vendor credit for sea = -$16k (4 * $4k). Net +$40k. Anticipate pallet/staging/inspection ~ $2k per sea pallet -> +$8k. Total net ~ +$48k.

Nate O'Connor: Also we still have 3 DOA units from last month's batch flagged in RMA. Lia, will Atlas cover return freight for those and prioritize replacements?

Lia (AtlasVendor): For the 3 DOA units from last month, Atlas will cover return freight and repair. Provide RMA tickets & we'll generate prepaid labels if returns go to our EU depot. For replacements we can prioritize 2 units by air next week if you confirm serials now.

Sana Ruiz: I'll upload the serials and open RMA tickets in Zendesk. Also request a customs hold instruction for the sea shipment: "HOLD AT IMPORTER — DO NOT RELEASE" until we attach warranty paperwork to avoid duty misclassification.

FreightCo-Rep: We can add the hold instruction but need the importer EORI and the shipment reference on the booking. Also note hold requests may trigger storage charges if extended.

Maya Chen: Action items: Lia send AWB numbers + full manifest by EOD; Lia confirm prepaid RMA labels for DOA and formalize the $4k credit for sea delay; Ops to finalize accept/decline for 8 air/4 sea by 09:00 UTC tomorrow. Chris loop finance for approval.

Zoe Park: tagging @ops-bot for a capacity recheck once AWBs are posted.

ops-bot: Capacity hold noted — reserved capacity stands until 09:00 UTC tomorrow pending AWB confirm.

Lia (AtlasVendor): One more option: if you confirm within 3 hours we can move 2 units from sea into air at +$6,500/unit (space-limited).

Maya Chen: Provisional decision: accept 8 air + 4 sea. If Atlas can secure those 2 extra air slots at quoted rate, notify ASAP and we'll consider. Thanks, all.
